content_blocks.text: DAULATABAD FORT
Daulatabad fort is located at Daulatabad village in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar ( Aurangabad ), Maharashtra
ABOUT

DAULATABAD FORT is a historical place which is also known as (Devgiri fort). It was built on a 200 meter high conical hill in the 12th century by King Yadava Bhillama V, and was named the Devgiri. The fort was renamed Daulatabad by Mohammed Tughlaq in the 14th century, according to historians. It is situated at Daulatabad in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra. The fort is very close to Ellora caves at 11 KM distance and from Shree Bhadra Maruti Temple at 13 KM. Daulatabad fort has been the capital of many dynasties, as the first capital of Yadava and, briefly, for the Delhi Sultanate. It has a scenic view and rich history. It is an attractive tourist destination with a rating of 4.5 & 21,000+ reviews.

SHREE LAKSHA VINAYAK GANAPATI TEMPLE
Shree Laksha Vinayak Ganapati Temple located at Verul village in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar ( Aurangabad) Maharashtra
ABOUT

The Shree Laksha Vinayak Ganapati Temple is a respected and spiritually considerable Temple which is dedicated to Lord Shri Ganesha and this temple murti is self-proclaimed who is worshiped as Laksha Vinayaka. Laksha means ‘1 lakh’ which indicates the Lord’s immense power and ability to fulfill wishes.

Devotees believe that worshiping Lord Laksh Vinayak here removes all Problem in life and confer success and prosperity. The temple has full of spiritual energy & olden traditions, and it is visited by thousands of devotees throughout the year. The clam atmosphere of the temple, the chanting of mantras and the ritualistic worship give a spiritual feel to everyone. This is the seventeenth seat among the twenty-one self-manifested Ganesha shrines in India
The temple is situated at Shree Kshetra Verul in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra. It is 5 to 10 minutes on walking distance from Shri Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga temple .

Shri Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga located at Verul village in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar ( Aurangabad) Maharashtra
About

It was first found in the 6th century and was rebuilt in the year 1729 by Queen Ahilyabai Holkar in its current state. It is the 12th and final jyotirlinga & namely known for its Hemadpanti Architectural beauty, meaningful history & spiritual significance of the Lord Shiva.

ABOUT

Panchakki Watermill is an attractive tourist site which is situated in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad) of Maharashtra. It was established in 1744 AD and built to generate electric energy from the water useful for grinding the grains of pilgrims by  Disciple of a Sufi saint, Hazrat Baba Shah Musafir. content_blocks.text: Shree Bhadra Maruti Temple
Shree Bhadra Maruti Temple is located at Khuldabad in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar ( Aurangabad) Maharashtra
ABOUT

Shree Bhadra Maruti Mandir is the oldest temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman ji where Lord Hanuman Ji is in a sleeping position. It is located at Khuldabad in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra.

The temple was found to have existed since the Ramayana period, and the old name of this temple used to be known as ‘Bhadravathi.’ The King of Bhadravathi used to be Bhadrasen, who was the Devotee of Lord Ram. Once the king of this place was singing hymns. While hearing the hymns, The Lord Hanumanji came to this place, and listening to the sweet hymns went in a sleeping posture. Seeing like this King Bhadra Sen Prayed to the Lord Hanumanji ji to stay here forever. After that, the temple was built in this place by King Bhadrasen.

This is one of the three temples in India where Lord Hanumanji can be seen in a resting posture, two of these temples are located in different places. The second one is at the banks of Ganga Sangam in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, and the third one is at Jam Sawali in Madhya Pradesh.

The temple is a spiritual site and a beautiful tourist attraction, as a large number of devotees reach there at the time of festivals like Hanuman Jayanti & Ram Navami. Many people arrive there from Aurangabad and nearby Village to take Darshan’s on Tuesday & Saturday also.
It is very close from Ellora Caves .

The primary purpose of this fort was to maintain military surveillance and security, protecting the major trade routes, especially those in the Nashik region.

It is very famous for the steep rock, and 117 rock cut stairs are made at an inclined angle of 80 degrees to climb up the hill, and there are small pits to grip to hold hands, from where you can easily climb upwards while holding the stairs’ pits, and it has the temple of Lord Hanuman and Lord Shiva on top of the hill.
The primary purpose of this fort was to maintain military surveillance and security, protecting the major trade routes, especially those in the Nashik region.
It is an attractive tourist site known for the great experience of trekking and knowledge of historical significance about the fort, and a huge number of people gather here during the rainy and winter seasons for hiking and to enjoy the stunning and breathtaking views of the surrounding Sahyadri mountains, Bhaskar gadh, Anjaneri Fort and Bramhagiri parvat.

You need to start in the early Morning (6:00 AM to 9:00 AM).
